aboutText:
hey, i'm artyom - developer, artist, and technical lead. i work across the stack: from low-level c++ and assembly to high-level c#, python, and web. my focus: the intersection of systems programming, reverse engineering, and visual creation.

i take a structured approach to every project - clear naming, clean pipelines, predictable revisions. whether it's analysing binaries in ida pro, building an opengl renderer, or animating a steam-loop, i hold the same line: technical rigour meets aesthetic intent.

currently technical director at noxyrium (minecraft server in development). training as a technical artist - next up: hlsl shaders at the art-engine boundary. also exploring 2d/3d animation, illustration, and stylized worlds in blender with goo engine.

experienceHtml.csharp: first real c# project. the language that taught me oop, async, and what "managed runtime" actually means. started with console apps and small tools.
experienceHtml.unity: built first playable games in unity with c#. learned scene structure, prefabs, coroutines, and the asset pipeline. shipped a couple of small prototypes.
experienceHtml.blender: picked up blender for 3d modelling, sculpting, and basic game dev. made my first environments and learned hard-surface modelling. set the foundation for the 3d side of the work.
experienceHtml.cpp: went low-level with c++ and system programming. memory management, build systems, and writing code that actually touches the metal. later fed straight into the engine work.
experienceHtml.reverse: reverse engineering work - reading binaries, mapping structures, writing tooling around disassembly. sharpened debugging instincts across all later work.
experienceHtml.opengl: building a low-level 3d rendering engine using modern opengl, glfw, glad, and glm. custom vertex and fragment shaders in glsl, mvp pipelines, lighting, geometry. the technical artist path runs through here.
experienceHtml.design: full design practice across visual identity, ui composition, typography, and branding. avatars, gfx assets, thumbnails, promo material via photoshop, after effects, and blender. experimenting with motion for dynamic visual content.
experienceHtml.animation: producing original animation in both 2d and 3d. in blender - full character/object rigging, keyframe animation, cinematic renders. in after effects - layer separation, compositing, motion graphics and video intros.
experienceHtml.drawing: learning to draw in anime style. anatomy, gesture, colour, stylisation. main tool is clip studio paint, with photoshop for processing. still practising character sketches and backgrounds.
experienceHtml.live2d: studying live2d for character rig and animation - the format used in vtuber and gacha workflows. building a portfolio piece around the toji character (see toji 2d in the portfolio section).
experienceHtml.website: designing and developing this portfolio site from scratch with vanilla html, css, and javascript - no frameworks. parallax video layers, language switching, sakura, custom cursor, effects toggle. live portfolio and a lab for pure front-end.
experienceHtml.northmine: worked as a developer on northmine.ru, a minecraft server project. server-side scripting, configuration, and small plugins. shipped in production, then moved on to noxyrium.
experienceHtml.maya: currently learning autodesk maya as a third 3d package alongside blender and after effects. focus on industry-standard rigging, character animation, and studio pipelines - so portfolio work in 3d ships in a professional workflow.
experienceHtml.ta: studying as a technical artist across unity, maya, and blender. writing custom shaders in glsl and hlsl, building render pipelines, and automating repetitive work through python scripts in maya and blender add-ons (geometry nodes, bpy, asset batchers, export pipelines). the bridge between code and art - and the boring parts that nobody wants to click through by hand.
experienceHtml.noxyrium: serving as technical director of noxyrium - an atmospheric minecraft server currently in active development. full technical vision: server architecture, performance optimisation, custom plugin development, infrastructure. coordinating the technical team.

flourite.title: Flourite
flourite.desc: Arknights: Endfield - Flourite as a detailed steam-loop. Illustration in motion over a painted field.
flourite.task: build a dynamic steam-loop for flourite - detailed character animation, not a still with a wobble.
steps: pre-production: the client art was split into many pieces. after the cut: 68 layers.
animation & fx: keyframes through the body and cloth; turbulence on the frame; blur and glow to hold the loop.
post: color, grain, glow, final render - export without clipping the edges.
flourite.problem: the comp got too heavy: too many effects in one timeline, too many unnamed layers to get lost in.
flourite.takeaway: structure first. name layers and precomps. split the work. export clean, no cropped pieces.

toji.title: Toji Avatar GFX
toji.desc: Personal social avatar - cold-blue neon character composition.
toji.task: Create a striking social avatar: cut out the character, integrate him into a new background, add lighting, overlays and atmosphere in a cold blue palette.
steps: Extracted the character and cleaned the edges
Matched him to a dark tech background
Added custom lighting, glow, overlays and color grading (cold blue)
Final contrast and sharpening pass
toji.problem: Hair had leftover artifacts and fringing after the cutout. Finding the right background + overlay combination took several iterations.
toji.takeaway: Always spend extra time on hair clean-up and edge refinement before adding heavy effects. Good lighting can hide minor flaws, but clean edges matter more.

tojil2d.title: Toji Live2D
tojil2d.desc: Live2D animation in progress - rig and motion for Toji Fushiguro. Separate from the GFX avatar.

greenvert.title: Zani Avatar GFX
greenvert.desc: Vertical character poster - toxic green atmosphere.
greenvert.task: Build a tall vertical piece with strong green color mood, energy effects and clear character focus (phone wallpaper / poster format).
steps: Character placement and posing
Heavy green color grading and fog/smoke atmosphere
Added particles, glow and background symbols
Final light wrap and contrast
greenvert.problem: Skin and legs got overexposed (blown out) because of too strong light layers.
greenvert.takeaway: Control highlights earlier. Use curves or selective light instead of stacking pure white glows.

banner.title: Gabimaru Banner GFX
banner.desc: Wide tech / cyber banner with character and custom typography.
banner.task: Design a clean wide banner (header style) in black and white tech aesthetic with strong branding and character presence.
steps: Character cutout + subtle outline/glow
Geometric tech elements, lines, dots and grid
Custom typography treatment (ZAZARY)
Final composition balance and soft light streaks
banner.problem: White stroke around the character felt slightly cheap on the shoulder area.
banner.takeaway: Soft light wrap or thin outer glow usually looks more premium than a hard dashed stroke.

benim.title: Benimaru Avatar GFX
benim.task: Make a dynamic blue-toned character piece with strong energy effects and a clear focal point.
steps: Character isolation
Blue lighting and rim light
Energy overlays, particles and atmosphere
Color grade + final polish
benim.problem: Effects could easily overpower the character if not controlled.
benim.takeaway: Always keep the face and upper body most readable - effects should support, not bury the subject.

gojo.title: Gojo Avatar GFX
gojo.desc: Square avatar / profile piece - chrome type + purple magic atmosphere.
gojo.task: Create a premium square composition with stylish chrome lettering and rich purple lighting.
steps: Character placement and lighting
Chrome-style text behind the figure
Purple energy, glow, particles and floral elements
Final color grade and vignette
gojo.problem: Looking back at the case, the suit is overexposed. This was my first time building a full composition and integrating a character into it, so the highlight balance was not controlled well enough.
gojo.takeaway: Check bright clothing separately before export. Character integration needs controlled highlights, local curves and a short break before the final review.

quest.title: Quest 3
quest.desc: Product key visual - Meta Quest 3 headset and controllers.
quest.task: Create a clean premium product shot of the Quest 3 with floating controllers, hexagon podium and strong blue tech atmosphere. No text, pure visual focus.
steps: Product placement and lighting setup
Hexagon podium + circular neon base
Controllers positioning and rim light
Dark blue environment, glow, reflections and final color grade
quest.problem: Earlier version had Russian feature callouts (source file was lost). Had to rebuild a clean text-free version.
quest.takeaway: Always keep layered sources. A strong product visual without text is more flexible - it works for any language and can later receive EN/RU text overlays if needed.

goo.title: Stylized Worlds
goo.desc: Learning stylized worlds in Blender with Goo Engine - look, lighting, and a painted 3D space.

maya.title: Learning Maya
maya.desc: On the roadmap: 3d modeling, animation, rigging. Preparing for production work in a studio.

anime.title: Anime Style
anime.desc: Learning to draw in anime style - anatomy, gesture, colour, stylization. Working in Clip Studio Paint.

aecompose.title: AE Compositing
aecompose.desc: Learning After Effects compositing for animation pieces - layers, masks, easing, sound sync. Queued - not live yet.

makima.title: Makima Avatar GFX
makima.desc: Aggressive red anime GFX cover with strong character presence, high-contrast FX and layered compositing.
makima.task: Design an aggressive red anime GFX banner/cover with strong character presence, high-contrast visual effects and heavy overlay compositing.
steps: AI Upscale & Retouch: upscaled the source with AI, then manually retouched it and repaired Makima’s eye after generation.
Composition Building: created the composition base, cut out the character, integrated large kanji into the background and built dynamic frames and boundaries.
Color Correction & Overlay Stacking: applied a deep red-and-black grade and carefully layered energy lightning, splashes, magic/blood effects and noise texture.
Final Lighting & Balance: unified every element and refined the accent lighting around the character’s hands and face.
makima.problem: After working with bright red and dense FX for a long time, the eye becomes desensitized. Overexposure, broken composition balance and unnecessary background clutter become easy to miss.
makima.takeaway: Take a 10–15 minute break before the final render and export. Rested eyes make lighting and focus problems immediately visible.

gojobot.title: Gojo Bot Avatar
gojobot.desc: Black-and-white manga avatar for the studio's commission bot — ink contrast over a deep blue cosmos.
gojobot.task: Design a Telegram bot avatar for the studio's commission bot: instantly readable at small size, recognizable in the dark Telegram UI, and tied to the black-and-white manga identity of the works.
steps: Render Base: prepared the soft full-color render as the source for proportions, lighting and the head tilt.
Style Conversion: rebuilt the piece in black-and-white manga style — ink contrast, hatching and graphic whites instead of color.
Background Building: composed the deep blue cosmic background with giant vertical kanji columns, particles and energy streaks.
Contrast Balance: tuned effects so the silhouette reads first and the atmosphere second — the avatar had to survive a tiny round crop.
gojobot.problem: Background selection and effect rearrangement kept fighting the soft, empathetic mood of the original render — every pass pulled the piece toward something cold and grandiose instead of warm and personal.
gojobot.takeaway: An avatar is judged at 56 px, not 2048. Test the crop in a real Telegram chat before polishing the background.

evelyn.title: Evelyn · Full Render
evelyn.desc: First piece where I painted a full environment by hand - path, lawn and stones. All 2D, no 3D base. Work in progress.
evelyn.task: Render the character together with the environment entirely in 2D - no 3D environments, working from knowledge and technique instead of models: grass, stones, flowers and shadows are drawn by hand.
steps: Character: body, skin, fabric and hair rendered from scratch - top light so the figure reads against the path.
Environment: lawn, path and kerb. Grass, trees and flowers were studied in parallel from tutorials on Rednote (xiaohongshu), Pinterest and reference material.
Stones and kerb: layering, silhouette and the small debris along the lawn edge.
Light and shadow: cast shadows from the figure and from objects in the scene.
evelyn.problem: At this stage I can see: the grass and flower patches come out chaotic and need smoothing, some stone shapes do not work yet, there are too few cast shadows, and the scene lacks props that complete it and hold the composition.
evelyn.takeaway: Build grass in clusters instead of single blades and calm the contrast in the background. Settle a stone's silhouette first, detail after. Shadows and the second plane belong in the blocking stage
evelyn.caseNote: The speedpaint drops once the piece is finished.
